predecessors.name: Chola Empire
predecessors.text: the island, which Cliopatria's Chola shape holds to 1093 and the Chola dossier closes in 1070

successors.name: Jaffna kingdom
successors.text: the northern realm (Rajarata, the Vanni and the Jaffna peninsula) that Magha kept after 1236

successors.name: Kingdom of Dambadeniya
successors.text: the Polonnaruwa core, from which Magha was expelled in 1236 'in a southern invasion'

ledger.x: By 1070: Sinhalese sovereignty is restored under Vijayabahu I.

c. 1153: Parakramabahu I reunites the island. 'Around 1150 AD, Parakramabahu made his first move' (taking Malaya); 'Following a protracted civil war, he secured power over the entire island around 1153'; he was crowned and became 'the unquestioned lord of the entire island'. The page gives the war's…

c. 1167: Sinhalese troops take Rameswaram in the Pandyan war. The Pandyan king 'appealed to his namesake in Sri Lanka for assistance'; the general Lankapura Dandanatha 'landed in the vicinity of Ramanathapuram' and 'captured the city of Rameswaram'. The Polonnaruwa page: Rameswaram…

Pandya kingdom of Madurai (Kulasekhara's side in the Pandyan civil war)

ledger.x: 1212: a Pandyan-backed claimant seizes the capital.

wars.name: Parakramabahu I's war of unification
wars.outcome: Parakramabahu I takes Malaya around 1150 and 'secured power over the entire island around 1153'; the three kingdoms of 1111 become one.

wars.name: Ruhuna revolt and the 1160 insurrection
wars.outcome: Put down; Ruhuna stayed quiet afterwards except for 'a brief insurrection in 1160' (Parakramabahu I page); the Polonnaruwa page calls the 1160 rising 'formidable'.

wars.name: Pandyan Civil War (Sinhalese intervention)
wars.outcome: The war 'ended in favour of the Cholas, sometime in the 1170s'; Rameswaram stayed under Sinhalese and Vira Pandyan rule until 1182.

wars.name: Rebellion at Mantota
wars.outcome: The only rebellion of the reign outside Ruhuna, 'in the region of modern Mantota in from 1168-1169'; no border moved.

wars.name: Pandyan claimant at Polonnaruwa
wars.outcome: Parakrama Pandyan II seizes the capital in 1212 with Pandyan help and reigns to 1215, when Magha invades.

wars.name: Kalinga Magha's invasion
wars.outcome: Magha 'invaded the kingdom with the help of his soldiers and mercenaries' in 1215 and ruled from the north until he was 'expelled from Polonnaruwa in 1236'.

certainty.note: Neither page draws a frontier; the island coast is the only hard edge, and Rajarata's southern limit is a stand-in.
